problem: The released busy diagnostic labels retained lock-file text active even when a different workload currently owns the kernel lock. Invalid retained text can also prevent the typed busy result.
requirements: Derive busy exclusively from the existing failed nonblocking kernel lock acquisition; retained bytes are not authenticated current execution ownership.
Do not read or echo retained lock bytes on refusal. Return the existing local_execution_busy_deferred code with explicitly unverified execution ownership.
Preserve the lock path, authenticated namespace derivation, nonblocking behavior, exact execution-ID validation, successful write/yield/release behavior and immutable retained bytes on refusal.
A refusal cannot enter work, unlock the actual holder, delete/recreate the lock, retry, allocate proof, push or select an alternative namespace.
Preserve CLI grammar and the existing typed busy code; retire only the unsupported active attribution. No new lease broker, owner registry or authority family.
verification: Real flock contention on a private unit-fixture file containing stale, undecodable and untrusted retained bytes; holder continuity, no work entry, byte preservation and successful reuse. Existing prospective exclusion oracle remains required.
limits: An unverified owner is not permission to remove/reset a lock.
This does not implement transaction coalescing or authenticate an execution subject from a PID.
